Create a sparse counterfactual by zeroing contradicting variables

bl_find_sparse_cf.Rd

Builds a sparse version of the boundary counterfactual by retaining only the variables whose Shapley contribution supports the prediction direction. Variables classified as "Contradicts" or "Unknown" revert to their observed values. Additionally, any variable constrained as "fixed" in set_filters always reverts to its observed value regardless of its Shapley classification, because the "fixed" constraint permits only a \(\pm 0.5\) search window and the observed value is the intended sparse target.

Usage

bl_find_sparse_cf(bl_shapley_result, round_to = NULL)

Arguments

bl_shapley_result

A "bl_shapley" object from bl_shapley.

round_to

Positive numeric or NULL. If not NULL, rounds supporting variable values to the nearest multiple of this value (e.g. round_to = 0.5 rounds to the nearest 0.5; round_to = 1 rounds to the nearest integer). Default NULL (no rounding).

Value

A list of class "bl_sparse_result" with the following fields:

x_sparse

Single-row data frame; the sparse counterfactual in X-space.

pred_sparse

Scalar predicted probability of the sparse CF.

solution_valid

Logical; TRUE if the sparse CF flips the predicted class.

shapley_df

The annotated Shapley data frame with columns used_in_sparse and x_sparse_val.

bl_shapley

The "bl_shapley" object passed in.
